AMBER DIAL-GLOW — warm amber daylight glows through the frosted clock-face, throwing reversed hand-shadows across the colossal brass gears behind.
ROSE-WINDOW DIAL — the translucent face glows like a stained-glass rose-window, its numerals shining silhouettes onto the meshing dark mechanism below.
MOONLIT DIAL — cold blue moonlight filters through the translucent dial, silvering the great gears and swinging pendulum in the night tower.
CRACKED-DIAL GOLD — gold light streams through the dial's hairline cracks, throwing bright needles of warmth across the dusty, motionless gear-hall within.
NUMERAL-SHADOW FALL — the great roman numerals cast their silhouettes as bars of glowing light deep across the turning cog-faces behind the dial.
DUST-SHAFT DIAL — a broad shaft of amber light through the clock-face catches slow-drifting gear-dust hanging golden in the dark mechanism's air.
HOUR-HAND RAKE — the reversed hour-hand's long shadow rakes hard across the cog-wheels, a dark spoke turning through the warm amber dial-light.
FROSTED MORNING DIAL — pale morning light blooms through the frosted glass face, filling the gear-hall with soft diffuse amber before the city wakes.
MINUTE-HAND SWEEP — the reversed minute-hand's thin shadow sweeps steadily across great brass gears, a slow dark needle in the dial's warm glow.
GEAR-HALL LANTERN — the self-lit clock-face burns like a single great lantern, pouring warm amber deep into the otherwise lightless tower mechanism.
DUSK-DIAL EMBER — the dial deepens to ember-orange at dusk, washing the entire gear-hall in furnace warmth before the blue night arrives.
BLUE MIDNIGHT FACE — cold blue midnight light floods the translucent dial, turning every brass gear-tooth to silver and every shadow to ink.
NUMERALS-ON-BRASS — amber light glowing through the dial prints the great numeral-shapes as luminous shadows across the polished faces of the drive-gears.
PENDULUM-SHADOW DIAL — the pendulum's silhouette sweeps the dial's amber glow rhythmically across the lower gear-train with every slow, metronomic tick.
CLOUDED-DIAL GREY — flat grey cloud-light through the translucent face drains the gear-hall of warmth, leaving the mechanism cold and colourless by noon.
STORM-DIAL FLARE — lightning beyond the dial floods the gear-hall with one sharp white burst, throwing every tooth and arbor into sudden relief.
GILT-CRACK RAYS — fine gold rays stream through the dial's gilded rim-cracks, striping the upper gear-train in warm lines across cold iron.
STAINED-AMBER FACE — the amber dial glows like honey held to sunlight, its warm translucence pooling across the great slow-turning main-wheel below.
WINTER-MOON DIAL — a hard winter moon burns through the dial, its blue-white light sharpening every gear-shadow into a precise, cold-edged silhouette.
DOUBLE-HAND CROSS — where the hour and minute hands cross, their shadows form a dark intersection raking across the warm gear-faces behind the dial.
DUSTY-SHAFT MORNING — morning light shafts through the lower dial-crack, catching a column of gear-dust rising slowly in the warm amber beam.
ROMAN-NUMERAL GLOW — the XII glows brightest at noon, its silhouette thrown long and golden across the topmost great-wheel in the tower's dark.
TWILIGHT DIAL-SHIFT — the dial passes through copper to violet at twilight, dragging the gear-hall's colour from warm brass-glow to cold shadow with it.
BACK-LIT MECHANISM — the dial's constant self-lit glow silhouettes every gear, arbor, and fly-wheel in warm amber against the dark tower behind them.
FULL-MOON FROST DIAL — full moonlight saturates the translucent face completely, flooding the gear-hall in cold blue so the brass gears read as grey iron.
